package.name: f1tenth_behavior
package.description: py_trees-based reactive safety-stop (obstacle corridor check onto the ackermann_mux), an emergency-stop lane (low battery / CPU-GPU overheating, from f1tenth_diagnostics' diagnostics_server_node and system_observer_node), plus Nav2 goal-pose navigation (NavigateThroughPoses, sent as a single-element poses list once a /goal_pose message is received -- no static waypoint list), plus a scripted mission subtree (JSON-config move sequences driving mpc_corr via /mpc/goal_distance and /mpc/hold, with per-move stop conditions and reactions to detected object classes -- see mission/ and the README's config table; loaded via the mission_file_name param, /mission/load_path topic, or the /mission/load_mission, /mission/start_mission, and /mission/abort_mission services -- state published on /mission/status), plus a latched, unconditional /mission/emergency_stop and a raw-sensor IsProximityTooClose (ZED depth + /scan, YOLO-independent) both feeding the emergency lane alongside battery/overheat, plus a live colored dot-graph of the running tree's status published on /bt/tree_visualization for the F1TENTH stack. Guarded behind stack_bringup's use_behavior_tree arg, mutually exclusive with mpc_controller's direct drive-command path. Depends on f1tenth_navigation's nav2.launch.py already being up (that package now owns all Nav2 node bring-up).
